_note: Forming a government after the election (rules/coalition.gd). Works with any number of parties. MINISTRIES: the posts shared out in a coalition; 'weight' is how much each is worth (the Prime Minister most), 'axes' the issues it serves: a party whose manifesto is strong on one of those wants it a little more (it picks it first when its turn comes). STANCE: how one party sees another, from their relation (-100..100): at or below 'enemy' they will never govern together, at or above 'ally' they join without asking for extra. Between the two they are neutral and want a better share. NEUTRAL_PREMIUM: how much more than its fair share (by seats) a neutral party asks for, as a fraction of the cabinet. SHUTOUT_RELAXES: after one party is shut out, the others' enmities count as neutral. MAX_FORMATEURS: how many parties, largest first, get to try in each round. FORMATEUR_GIVES: how much of its own fair share the party forming the government will give up to close a deal (0.4 = up to 40%). DEMAND_SLACK: when a party asks you to join, it accepts demands worth up to this much of your fair share (more for a neutral partner), without haggling. PM_PRICE: it hands you the Prime Minister's office only when desperate (a coalition with you alone is its only way in, and the others could govern without it), and then only if your other demands come to at most this much of your fair share. FAVOURITE_WORTH: each party has two favourite ministries (content.json PARTIES 'ministries', or the two serving its strongest issues), worth this many times their weight to it. OPENING_ASK: when you are the largest party and bargain yourself, partners open by asking this much more than they need (they accept a final offer that gives them what they need). COMPROMISE: when every try fails only because partners asked too much, but a majority without enemies exists, the largest party in one forms it anyway and every member takes its fair share by seats. LINES_PER_MINISTRY: instead of ministries you can give a partner its own line on an issue in the coalition agreement (where your manifestos differ); an average ministry is worth this many lines.

COLUMN._note: The ending is an opinion column about your campaign: who writes it, and where.
COLUMN.author: Ilse Marrow

OUTCOMES._note: How the election ended for the player: a headline and the feeling of it. Placeholders: {party}, {leader}. First drafts; the end screens are still to be designed.

majority.headline: {party} wins a majority
majority.line: No partners and no compromises: the country is yours to shape.

leads.headline: {leader} to lead a coalition
leads.line: The largest party and the Prime Minister's office. Now comes governing with partners who want their share of every decision.

senior.headline: {party} governs, but gives up the top job
senior.line: The largest party in the new government, but the Prime Minister's office was the price of the deal.

pm.headline: {leader} becomes Prime Minister
pm.line: The top job is yours, though yours is not the largest party. It still has a long way to go.

partner.headline: {party} joins the government
partner.line: A junior partner: one cog in someone else's machine, with the chance to show what you can do in office.

opposition.headline: {party} left in opposition
opposition.line: Others will govern. Time to look in the mirror and prepare better for the next election.

robbed.headline: {party} wins the vote, loses the country
robbed.line: The voters made you the largest party. The back rooms decided otherwise.

no_seats.headline: {party} fails to enter parliament
no_seats.line: Not one seat. The country heard of you; not enough of it voted for you.

deadlock.headline: No government for {country}
deadlock.line: No one could form a government. The country will have to vote again.

TEXT.neutral_refuses_you: Neutral: you want more than {f} can give, and walk away.
